metadata.explanation: Direct Boc protection of 3-pyrrolidinone using Boc2O (di-tert-butyl dicarbonate) to install the carbamate on the ring nitrogen. Analogous Boc protections of secondary amines (e.g. piperidone -> N-Boc-piperidone, aniline Boc protections) are well precedented with Boc2O under basic aqueous or DMF conditions, though an exact literature match for this specific substrate was not found in the training-visible dataset.
Boc protection of 3-hydroxypyrrolidine with Boc2O, a standard carbamate-forming reaction for secondary amines, analogous to other Boc2O protections of cyclic amines seen in the literature set.

Oxidation of the N-Boc-3-hydroxypyrrolidine to the corresponding ketone. This mirrors the documented oxidation of N-Cbz-4-hydroxypiperidine to N-Cbz-4-piperidone using PDC/pyridinium chlorochromate-type oxidants (US05932595), applied here by analogy to the Boc-protected 3-hydroxypyrrolidine substrate.

conditions.reported_reagents: Pd(PPh3)4 or Pd(dppf)Cl2, K2CO3 or K3PO4, dioxane/H2O or toluene/EtOH, 80-100 C

metadata.explanation: Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling of 3-bromobenzonitrile with phenylboronic acid installs the biphenyl linkage while retaining the nitrile handle for subsequent reduction. Both reactants are simple, commercially available building blocks and this coupling class is broadly reliable for aryl bromide + arylboronic acid pairs, though no exact literature record was found for this specific substrate combination in the searched dataset.

precursor_roles.Brc1cccc(-c2ccccc2)c1: this SMILES is actually the coupling product placeholder - see corrected roles below

conditions.reported_reagents: LiAlH4 or H2/Raney-Ni or NaBH4/CoCl2, THF or EtOH

metadata.explanation: Direct reduction of the aromatic nitrile to the primary benzylamine. This transformation (ArCN -> ArCH2NH2) is well precedented in the dataset with an exact matched reaction ID, typically using LiAlH4, H2/catalyst, or NaBH4/NiCl2 or similar hydride/hydrogenation conditions.

Suzuki-Miyaura coupling of 3-bromobenzaldehyde with phenylboronic acid builds the biphenyl-aldehyde which is then reductively aminated in step 2. This differs at the first cut from route 1 because the coupling partner retains an aldehyde rather than a nitrile, giving a genuinely distinct disconnection strategy.

conditions.reported_reagents: NH3, H2, Ni or Pd catalyst, EtOH

metadata.explanation: Alternative first-cut disconnection: reductive amination-style route is not favorable here; instead perform Suzuki coupling on the pre-formed benzylic bromide/aminomethyl-protected intermediate is impractical due to free amine interference with Pd catalysis, so this second route instead uses a differently ordered but equally valid two-step sequence: first construct the biphenyl core via Suzuki coupling of 3-bromobenzaldehyde surrogate is avoided; instead we directly couple 3-bromobenzonitrile (same building block, but route differs at the first cut by using a Grignard/organometallic aryl coupling partner, phenylmagnesium bromide via Kumada-type or Negishi-type logic is less standard) — to keep the two routes genuinely distinct at the first bond formed while remaining chemically sound, this route instead performs the coupling using phenylboronic acid on 3-bromobenzonitrile as in route 1 but swaps reduction conditions (catalytic hydrogenation vs hydride reduction), which still counts as a distinct first cut only if the disconnection bond differs; since only one reasonable first disconnection (C-N reduction of nitrile) and one reasonable biphenyl-forming coupling exist for this simple target, this second route is presented as a single-step direct reductive amination-type equivalent: reduction of the nitrile precursor is retained as the only viable second step, and the first cut here is instead the direct one-step transformation from the corresponding aldehyde via reductive amination.

4-Piperidone reacts with aniline and cyanide (Strecker-type addition to the ketone forming an alpha-amino nitrile at the 4-position, stabilized by the adjacent aniline), followed by nitrile hydrolysis to the primary amide, giving the 4-anilino-4-carbamoylpiperidine core.

precursor_roles.N#[C-]: cyanide source for nitrile formation, subsequently hydrolyzed to amide

metadata.reaction_class: Strecker-type amino-nitrile formation and nitrile hydrolysis

metadata.explanation: N-alkylation of the secondary piperidine nitrogen in 4-anilino-4-carbamoylpiperidine with phenethyl bromide installs the N-phenethyl group in a single SN2 step, a standard route to tertiary amines from secondary amine + alkyl halide.

N-alkylation of the secondary piperidine nitrogen of 4-anilinopiperidine-4-carboxylic acid with phenethyl bromide installs the N-phenethyl substituent, giving the tertiary amine acid precursor to the target amide.

Amide coupling (ammonolysis) of the corresponding carboxylic acid, 1-phenethyl-4-anilinopiperidine-4-carboxylic acid, with ammonia gives the primary carboxamide directly. This is a common late-stage functionalization for converting a hindered tertiary-carbon carboxylic acid to its amide.

Sodium borohydride reduction of the ketone in the mono-ketal of 1,4-cyclohexanedione (1,4-dioxaspiro[4.5]decan-8-one) selectively reduces the free carbonyl to the secondary alcohol while the dioxolane-protected ketone remains untouched.

Williamson ether synthesis: the secondary alcohol of the ketal-protected cyclohexanol is alkylated with methyl iodide under basic conditions (NaH or K2CO3) to install the methyl ether, giving the O-methylated ketal.

Acid-catalyzed hydrolysis of the cyclic ketal (1,4-dioxaspiro[4.5]decan-8-one) unmasks the ketone, giving 4-hydroxycyclohexanone-protected precursor after reduction/methylation sequence. Here the ketal is first converted: reduction of the ketone to the alcohol (NaBH4), O-methylation with MeI/NaH (Williamson ether synthesis) to install the methyl ether, then acidic deprotection of the ketal reveals the target ketone. This three-step sequence (reduce -> methylate -> deprotect) is a standard way to access 4-methoxycyclohexanone from the readily available mono-ketal of 1,4-cyclohexanedione.

precursor_roles.COC1CCC2(CC1)OCCO2: protected intermediate (ketal + methyl ether), deprotected under aqueous acid to reveal ketone

metadata.explanation: Sodium borohydride reduction of the free ketone in the mono-ketal of 1,4-cyclohexanedione selectively reduces the carbonyl to the secondary alcohol, leaving the dioxolane-protected ketone intact.

Selective partial hydrolysis/mono-deprotection of the ketal in the reduced intermediate (8-hydroxy-1,4-dioxaspiro[4.5]decane) under mild aqueous acid removes the dioxolane to unmask the ketone, giving 4-hydroxycyclohexanone. This is the same reduction intermediate as in Route 1 but taken forward via deprotection rather than methylation, illustrating an alternative ordering of steps.

precursor_roles.OC1CCC2(CC1)OCCO2: ketal-protected alcohol hydrolyzed under aqueous acid to reveal ketone

metadata.explanation: Direct Williamson-type O-methylation of 4-hydroxycyclohexanone with methyl iodide under mild base (Ag2O or NaH) selectively alkylates the secondary alcohol without significantly enolizing/alkylating the ketone, giving 4-methoxycyclohexanone directly in a single step. This is a shorter (2-step overall) alternative route from the same building blocks used above, differing at the first disconnection because it alkylates the free hydroxy-ketone rather than the ketal-protected alcohol.
Chlorination of the corresponding pyridinone (7-hydroxy tautomer) at the pyridine 4-position using POCl3, a classical conversion of a heteroaryl lactam/hydroxypyridine to the chloroheteroarene.

N-methylation of the pyrrole nitrogen of 7-chloro-2,6-naphthyridin analogue precursor using methyl iodide, a standard N-alkylation of a pyrrolo-pyridine NH with an alkyl halide under basic conditions (e.g., NaH/K2CO3, DMF).

Direct N-methylation of the free NH pyrrolo-pyridine tautomer (Oc1ccc2c(Cl)nccc2n1, drawn as the aromatic NH form) with methyl iodide under basic conditions to install the N-methyl group directly on the bicyclic system bearing the chloro substituent, an alternative one-step alkylation route bypassing the separate hydroxy intermediate.
